ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Geronimo — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Eleven-week review: therapy progress, sertraline and sodium, drinking and falls

text.paragraph: Eleven-week review: therapy, sertraline, drinking and falls. [S]

Geronimo returns eleven weeks after intake, with the interpreter. He has had eight sessions of cognitive processing therapy; he missed one when he had bronchitis three weeks ago, which has cleared without antibiotics. He has taken sertraline 25 mg for five weeks without nausea or dizziness. The sodium test planned for two to four weeks after starting was not done: it was not ordered at the sick visit, and today's test is the first. Nightmares come about twice a week and he sleeps five or six hours. He takes a single drink on one or two evenings a week and has had no heavy evening since the last visit. He has not fallen. [S]

The sodium check due two to four weeks after starting sertraline was missed: it was not ordered at the sick visit two weeks after the start, the one visit in that window. Done today at five weeks: 137 mmol/L, so no harm resulted, and he had no symptoms of low sodium. Corrective action: a laboratory-only visit is booked two weeks after any future SSRI dose change, and the clinic's SSRI order set now prompts the sodium check
